EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Discussions surrounding a potential US-Iran preliminary agreement, or Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), have intensified over the past 24 hours, with reports indicating a broad outline approval by Mojtaba Khamenei. However, significant disagreements persist on key clauses, particularly regarding Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile, the immediate release of frozen assets, and the extent of Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz. This situation is viewed with deep concern by Israeli officials, who warn the deal could be "catastrophic" and undermine regional stability.

IRAN
Discussions on a potential US-Iran preliminary agreement are ongoing, with US officials suggesting Mojtaba Khamenei approved the broad outline. However, Iranian sources like Tasnim and an unnamed senior official deny agreement to hand over highly enriched uranium, with some asserting the nuclear issue is not part of the preliminary deal and that Iran will not concede its red lines for the people's rights. Conflicting reports from US and Iranian sources detail the MOU's potential terms, including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, lifting of US naval blockades, and the release of frozen Iranian assets, with figures ranging from $6 billion to $25 billion. Iran's IRGC Navy reported 33 ships transited the Strait of Hormuz in the last 24 hours after obtaining Iranian approval, and shot down an Israeli "Orbiter" reconnaissance drone over Hormozgan province. Internally, Iran executed Mojtaba Kian for allegedly providing defense industry intelligence to the "American-Zionist enemy" and Mojtaba Kalani for similar intelligence. Mohsen Rezaei, an advisor to the Supreme Leader, warned Iran would exit the NPT and break any naval blockade if attacked again. The Tehran Prosecutor announced 13 arrests related to currency and trustee cases, and Mohammad Sarafraz claimed the regime acquired Chinese equipment to cut global internet access. Military exercises were conducted in Kish and controlled demolitions of unexploded ordnance from "Ramadan War" or US-Zionist attacks took place in Qom and Bandar Abbas.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the multi-dimensional unit killing four Hezbollah militants in southern Lebanon and destroying a 100-meter underground tunnel. In Gaza, the IDF killed Hamas sniper Luai Hasham Mahmoud Bazal, who participated in the October 7 attack on Zikim base, and destroyed several Hamas weapons depots in central Gaza containing anti-tank rockets, RPGs, and explosives. The Israeli home front experienced multiple hostile aircraft intrusion alerts across the Northern Command, particularly in Western Galilee, Kiryat Shmona, Avivim, Yir'on, Adamit, Shlomi, Ya'ara, Arab al-Aramshe, Eilon, Hanita, Shomera, Shtula, and Even Menachem, with interceptors fired, targets lost, and no reported casualties in most incidents, although an explosive drone from Hezbollah detonated on Israeli territory. Casualties included two Israeli Air Force pilots, Yuval Inbar (50) and Itai Talmi (72), killed in a light aircraft crash in the Jezreel Valley. Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu stated he and Trump agreed any final deal with Iran must dismantle nuclear enrichment facilities and remove enriched material, reiterating Israel’s right to self-defense in all fronts, including Lebanon. IDF Chief of Staff affirmed readiness for immediate intense fighting to weaken Iran and deepen damage to Hezbollah. President Herzog condemned a "horrific wave of violence by an anarchistic mob in Judea and Samaria" and stated that prisoners, however detestable, should not be abused. Coalition discussions continue on a conscription exemption law, facing opposition, and MK Yaakov Margi announced he will not run in the next elections after 23 years. Opinion polls show Netanyahu's chances of forming the next government at 33%, with Bennett at 42%.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli airstrikes in central Gaza killed a family of three and five police officers, with Halawa camp in Jablia under constant fire. The IDF successfully targeted and destroyed several Hamas weapons depots in central Gaza. Hamas sniper Luai Hasham Mahmoud Bazal, who participated in the October 7 attack on Zikim, was eliminated by Southern Command forces. Palestinians in Gaza face Israeli restrictions on performing the Hajj pilgrimage. President Herzog condemned violence by "anarchistic mobs" in Judea and Samaria, where military commanders are reportedly spending significant time managing criminal activities. A soldier en route to Lebanon for reserve duty was seen in Jerusalem with a weapon and a Torah scroll dedicated to the Yaniv brothers, killed in Huwara.

LEBANON
Hezbollah announced targeting an Israeli warplane over southern Lebanon with a surface-to-air missile and claimed to have shot down a Zionist drone in the western sector. They also released footage of Ababil attack drone operations targeting Israeli military vehicles, including a Merkava tank, a Nemira armored vehicle, and a communications vehicle in Taybeh, Deir Seryan, and Hadatha. An explosive drone launched by Hezbollah also detonated on Israeli territory near the border, causing minor injuries to two soldiers. The IDF launched a series of strikes in southern Lebanon, with warnings issued for residents in Nabatieh and Sidon areas. Confirmed Israeli airstrikes hit Zabdin, Ansar, and Sukhmore. IDF Chief of Staff stated approval of plans to "deepen the damage to Hezbollah" and affirmed readiness for intense fighting. Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem reiterated the group would never accept disarmament, asserting it would lead to a "new Israeli genocide," and criticized the Lebanese government's diplomatic failures with Israel, insisting that Hezbollah maintains its weapons until the government is fully independent. Reports indicate the potential US-Iran MOU includes an end to Israel-Hezbollah hostilities in Lebanon, a clause Israel is pushing to modify to preserve its freedom of action.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, violent clashes erupted between Al-Jolani gangs and residents in Tarhin, Aleppo province. In Iraq, the Counter-Terrorism Service announced three fighters martyred and four injured by an ISIS remnant explosive in the Al-Hadhar desert, Nineveh. A landmine explosion in Al-Tayyib, Maysan, killed one person. Explosions were reported in Samawah, northern Baghdad (Tarmiyah), and Erbil, with a security source attributing the Tarmiyah incident to a war remnant exploding due to a trash fire. Russia launched significant missile and drone attacks on Ukraine, including the use of "Oreshnik" ballistic and "Zircon" hypersonic missiles, targeting Kyiv and other areas, in retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on a school in Russia. Ukrainian forces claimed to have shot down 55 of 90 missiles and 549 of 600 drones. A fire broke out in a mountainous border area between Iraq and Iran in Sulaymaniyah province.

GULF STATES
Bahrain sentenced nine individuals to life imprisonment for cooperating with Iran's Revolutionary Guard and plotting terrorist acts. Iranian state media, citing the Financial Times, reported that the IRGC acquired Chinese satellite communications equipment via a trading network in the UAE (Ras al-Khaimah) in late 2025, used in its drone and missile programs, with GPS spoofing to conceal deliveries. US air refueling aircraft (KC-135R and KC-46A) were reportedly evacuated from Al Dhafra air base in the UAE, possibly redeploying to Israel or Saudi Arabia. US President Trump held "very good" calls with leaders from Saudi Arabia (Mohammed bin Salman), UAE (Mohammed bin Zayed), Qatar (Tamim bin Hamad, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, Ali Al-Thawadi), Jordan (King Abdullah II), and Bahrain (King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa) regarding a "peace MOU" with Iran, which regional leaders reportedly supported. However, Ayatollah Abbas Kaabi, a member of Iran's Assembly of Experts, accused some Gulf states of oppressing Shiites under the guidance of the US and Israel, and "Labaik Khamenei" chants were reported near the Interior Ministry in Manama, Bahrain.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran MOU Negotiations Intensify:** Reports from US officials, corroborated by CBS, suggest Mojtaba Khamenei approved the broad outline of a preliminary US-Iran agreement (MOU) for a 60-day period.
2.  **Conflicting Terms on Nuclear & Sanctions:** Major discrepancies exist between US and Iranian reports on the MOU details; US officials claim Iran agreed to dispose of highly enriched uranium and that sanctions relief is contingent on nuclear concessions, while Iranian sources deny any nuclear commitments in this phase and demand immediate release of frozen assets.
3.  **Israeli Opposition to Iran Deal:** Prime Minister Netanyahu and senior Israeli security officials expressed deep concern, with the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper citing a senior official calling the current deal "catastrophic" for Israel, fearing a loss of leverage.
4.  **Northern Front Escalation:** Israeli forces eliminated four Hezbollah militants and destroyed a 100-meter tunnel in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah launched an explosive drone into Israeli territory, injuring two soldiers, and claimed targeting an Israeli warplane and multiple military vehicles with Ababil drones.
5.  **Israeli Drone Downed in Iran:** Iran's IRGC, via Mehr News, claimed to have shot down an Israeli "Orbiter" reconnaissance drone over its southern Hormozgan province.
6.  **Iranian Executions:** Iran executed Mojtaba Kian and Mojtaba Kalani for allegedly providing intelligence to the US and Israel, with Kian’s case being fast-tracked in less than 50 days from arrest to execution.
7.  **Northern Israeli Civilian Alerts:** Multiple hostile aircraft intrusions into northern Israeli territories triggered alerts, leading to Israeli interceptor launches but with contact lost on targets, and no reported casualties.
8.  **Russian Ballistic Missile Attacks on Ukraine:** Russia conducted significant strikes on Ukraine using advanced "Oreshnik" intermediate-range ballistic missiles and "Zircon" hypersonic missiles, reportedly in retaliation for Ukrainian attacks.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The primary escalation risk stems from the highly contentious US-Iran MOU negotiations. Disagreements over key clauses, particularly Iran's nuclear program and its control over the Strait of Hormuz, could lead to a collapse of talks, potentially triggering renewed military hostilities. Iranian warnings of exiting the NPT and breaking naval blockades if attacked represent a significant red line. Israel's expressed concerns about the deal compromising its freedom of action in Lebanon further heighten regional tensions, especially given the ongoing intense cross-border exchanges with Hezbollah. The IDF Chief of Staff's readiness for "immediate intense fighting" and plans to "deepen damage to Hezbollah" suggest a high potential for a broader conflict on the northern front. The persistent hostile aircraft intrusions into northern Israel, even if not causing casualties, indicate an active flashpoint. Internally, Israel's political instability regarding the conscription law and the President's condemnation of settler violence add to the volatile environment, while Iran's continued missile development and active intelligence operations against its adversaries remain a concern.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US President Trump has been a central figure, announcing "good calls" with several regional leaders (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain) and Netanyahu regarding a "peace MOU" with Iran, which he claims is "largely negotiated." However, he maintains that the blockade on Iran will remain until an agreement is "reached, approved, and signed," and insists Iran will not develop nuclear weapons. US officials like Marco Rubio acknowledge "significant but not final progress" but warn against rushing, while former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo critically called the potential deal a "pay IRGC to build WMDs" scenario. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer welcomed progress, emphasizing an end to conflict and Hormuz reopening. Russia's Ambassador to Vienna, Mikhail Ulyanov, stated that dismantling Iran's nuclear program would be against the NPT. China reportedly proposed an initiative for an Iran-US deal focusing on a regional security framework without US presence, ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, asset unfreezing, and partial sanctions lifting, with Pakistan acting as a key mediator and potentially announcing details soon. Fifteen Muslim countries, including Egypt, Jordan, and Qatar, condemned Somaliland's embassy opening in Jerusalem as a violation of international law. French President Macron unusually spoke with Belarusian President Lukashenka. Turkey experienced internal clashes as police stormed the main opposition CHP headquarters following a court order. Pakistan reported a deadly train attack by the Balochistan Liberation Army. The US Embassy in Ukraine issued a major air attack warning, advising citizens to seek shelter, as Russia continued heavy missile and drone strikes. The EU is reportedly considering expanding sanctions on Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the terms and status of the US-Iran MOU. While Trump and some US officials suggest Iran has agreed to dispose of highly enriched uranium and that the Strait of Hormuz will open freely, Iranian sources explicitly deny agreeing to transfer enriched uranium and assert the Strait will remain under Iranian management, with traffic volume merely returning to pre-war levels under Iranian control. The exact amount of frozen assets to be released also varies significantly across reports ($6B, $25B, most funds only after final nuclear deal). There are unverified claims regarding Mojtaba Khamenei's status, with one source questioning his survival after an alleged attack on his residence, citing unusual handwriting in a condolence message. Propaganda is evident from multiple sides: Iranian state media promotes narratives of "Iran's ascendancy" and "US hegemony collapse," depicting the "Third Imposed War" as a victory, while some Israeli media claim "Trump surrenders to Iran." The opposition figure Omid Dana consistently dismisses all deal talks as a "game" by Trump, predicting inevitable war and regime collapse, which should be viewed through the lens of his activist stance. Reporting gaps include the full details and impact of Iran's "Lion's Roar" cyber campaign, the precise nature of "unexploded ordnance" in Iran's south, and whether alleged Israeli "top commander" casualties are confirmed. The identity of the "flotilla provocateurs" involved in the Spanish police incident and their objectives are also not fully detailed.
